source.title: Persona Non Grata: Single-Method Safety Evaluation Is Incomplete for Persona-Imbued LLMs
source.authors: Wenkai Li; Fan Yang; Shaunak A. Mehta; K. Onoue

page_placements.theme: Semantic framing, persona and social pressure alter safety

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests persona-based prompting and activation steering, not the fine-tuning, token-position KL, opening-prefill, suffix/decoding, weight-localization, or safety-deepening interventions specified in V1–V7. Its reported results concern persona-induced safety outcomes and related geometric measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports unsafe-response rates under persona prompting and activation steering, plus activation-geometry measurements. These are relevant to persona-induced safety risk but do not test any listed claim version. The per-persona tables, per-domain breakdowns, and additional coefficient and calibration analyses contain further persona-specific results; selected aggregate and illustrative results are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-response rates under persona system prompts, few-shot persona exemplars and CAA activation steering on instruct and reasoning models. None of these is fine-tuning (V1/V2), per-token KL by position (V3), prefill, suffix or decoding attacks (V4), weight or rank localization (V5), causes of shallowness (V6) or deepening training (V7). Qi et al. 2024 is cited only in related work, as evidence that safety sits in sparse neurons and shallow layers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Single-method persona safety evaluation is incomplete: prompting and activation steering give different, architecture-dependent vulnerability profiles, shown by the prosocial persona paradox. Reasoning gives only graded protection, and the trait–refusal alignment account is Llama-specific.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates persona system prompts, few-shot persona exemplars, and contrastive activation addition; it does not apply the original fine-tuning or token-position measurement recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies substantially by model and imbuing method. Steering coefficient also changes ASR and the strength of persona-rank inversion; persona-free few-shot exemplars lower ASR relative to the unadorned baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Persona-induced ASR depends on the imbuing method and the architecture. Llama-3.1-8B is most vulnerable to activation steering (0.618), Gemma and Qwen to system prompting. P12 has ASR 0.038 under SP but 0.818 under matched-strength AS on Llama, and 60% under AS on DeepSeek-R1-Distill.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona safety rankings and unsafe-response rates can invert between prompt-based and activation-steering persona imbuing, in an architecture-dependent way.

fits_no_version.finding: Reasoning models keep 15–18% prompt-side ASR under personas. Activation steering at α=4.0 gives 28.8% ASR for the neutral persona on DeepSeek-R1-Distill versus 9.4% on QwQ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chain-of-thought reasoning provides graded, model-dependent protection against persona-induced unsafe outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Persona-free benign few-shot exemplars give ASR 0.028 versus 0.033 with no persona and no exemplars, on Llama-3.1-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign in-context exemplars slightly lower unsafe-response rates. This is not a fine-tuning result.

fits_no_version.finding: Activations from prompting and from steering have low cosine similarity (0.11–0.20) at layers 21–23. Conscientiousness vectors are anti-aligned with the refusal direction on Llama (−0.164).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona steering vectors can geometrically oppose the refusal direction, in a model-specific way.

record.problems: The authors note that the prompt-versus-steering comparison is not fully causally factorized, the refusal-alignment framework is model-specific, some high-strength steering outputs can be incoherent, and the study focuses on open-weight models in single-turn settings with extreme trait poles. Some reasoning-trace diagnostics are heuristic.
record.rows_left_out: The complete per-persona tables for the four standard models (Appendix E, Tables 6–9), per-domain results (Tables 10–12 and 31), coefficient-ablation values (Table 24), and other per-persona robustness comparisons are not separately catalogued here; they are persona-specific outcomes outside V1–V7.

untested.parts: No benign-data fine-tuning. The benign few-shot exemplars are in-context only, not training.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models.
No compliant-prefill, adversarial-suffix or decoding-change attacks. Activation steering is applied at all positions as a persona intervention, not as an opening bypass.
No weight or rank localization. The trait-vs-refusal-direction cosines are activation-space measures.
No analysis of whether the data or the objective causes shallowness.
No deepening training or its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation (cites_only) and tranche (T6) are confirmed. Rows r1–r12 list baseline as not stated, although the P25 neutral SP baselines are in Tables 6–9 (e.g. 0.033 on Llama). This is a minor omission, and the rows bear on no version either way.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and whether it removes refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and whether it raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.

Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or whether any of these bypass refusal. Activation steering is tested as a persona intervention, not as one of these claimed bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives produce safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether such training holds up.

relation.reason: Related work cites shallow safety and localized safety computation; the study's own experiments concern persona interventions rather than the claim versions.

tranche.reason: Persona prompting and activation steering measure method-dependent safety vulnerability without testing or using any of V1–V7.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Table 1 prompt-side aggregates exclude P25 despite the study evaluating 25 persona configurations overall; Table 27 supports r20, while Table 6 reports slightly different P12 prompt-side values.
